DEPARTED KMCI GATE 0050Z.  UTILIZED RUNWAY 1R.  WEATHER WAS APPROXIMATELY 2500 OVERCAST WITH GOOD VISIBILITY.  FIRST OFFICER MATTHEW CARTWRIGHT WAS PILOT FLYING.  JUST AS AIRCRAFT WAS CLIMBING OUT OF A CLOUD LAYER AT APPROXIMATELY 4000 FT. A LARGE FLOCK OF BIRDS APPEARED.  THE CAPTAIN CALLED "BIRDS" BUT THERE WAS NO TIME TO TRY ANY EVASIVE MANEUVER.  THE FLOCK PASSED UNDER THE COCKPTI AND THE FLIGHT CREW INITIALLY THOUGHT THAT THEY HAD MISSED THEM.  THEY IMMEDIATELY FELT SEVERAL IMPACTS, APPROXIMATELY 5 TO 7.  BOTH ENGINES ROLLED BACK AND THE #2 ENGINE BEGAN COMPRESSOR STALLING.  THEY IMMEDIATELY STOPPED CLIMB AND STARTED TO RETARD THE #2 THROTTLE.  AS THEY PITCHED OVER TO STOP THEIR CLIMB, THE AUTOTHROTTLE REDUCED POWER TO BOTH ENGINES AND THE COMPRESSOR STALLING CEASED.  THEY CONTACTED KANSAS CITY DEPARTURE CONTROL AND DECLARED AN EMERGENCY, STATING MULITPLE BIRD STRIKES AND POSSIBLE DAMAGE TO BOTH ENGINES, AND REQUESTED IMMEDIATE RETURN TO KMCI, WHICH WAS PROVIDED.  ATC REQUESTED SOULS ON BOARD AN ASKED WHAT ELSE THEY NEEDED.  FLIGHT CREW REQUESTED THAT EMERGENCY EQUIMPMENT BE STANDING BY FOR THEIR ARRIVAL.  THEY CONSIDERED SHUTTING DOWN THE #2 ENGINE, BUT DECIDED NOT TO BECAUSE IT SEEMED TO OPERATE FINE AT LOWER POWER SETTINGS, AND ALSO BECAUSE THEY THOUGHT THE #1 ENGINE WAS DAMAGED DUE TO THE INITIAL ROLLBACK.  AS SOON AS THE AIRPLANE WAS TURNED BACK TO THE AIRPORT, AND THEIR SITUATION SEEMED TO BE IN CONTROL, THEY CONTACED THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS TO EXPLAIN THAT THEY HAD ENCOUNTERED MULTIPLE BIRD STRIKES AND WOULD BE RETURNING TO KMCI.  THEY TOLD THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS THAT THEY HAD APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES TO PREPARE THE CABIN FOR LANDING BUT THERE WAS NO NEED TO BRIEF THE PASSENGERS FOR BRACE AS THEY WERE EXPECTING A NORMAL LANDING.  AFTER BRIEFING THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS, THEY USED THE PA TO BRIEF THE PASSENGERS ON THE SITUATION. THEY WERE VECTORED FOR ILS 1L, DESCENDED JUST BELOW CLOUDS AT APPROXIMATELYLY 3000 FT AND LANDED VISUALLY.  THE AIRCRAFT WEIGHED 140,000# UPON LANDING - APPROXIMATELY 140 KTS.  THE CAPTAIN FELT THAT SINCE THE FIRST OFFICER WAS HANDLING THE SITUATION WELL, HE SHOULD CONTINUE FLYING, WHICH WOULD ALLOW HIM TO MONITOR THE AIRCRAFT FOR ANY FURTHER MALFUNCTIONS.  THE LANDING WAS VERY SMOOTH AND THE AIRCRAFT EXITED AT THE FIRST HIGH SPEED RUNWAY EXIT.  AFTER TURNOFF, THEY SHUT DOWN THE #2 ENGINE BECAUSE OF THE KNOWN DAMAGE AND TAXIED THE AIRCRAFT TO THE GATE.  THEY LEFT THE FLAPS DOWN BECAUSE OF SUSPECTED AIRFRAME DAMAGE.  THE BRAKES DID NOT OVERHEAT, EVEN AFTER THE HIGH SPEED LANDING.  THE FIRE DEPARTMENT FOLLOWED THE AIRCRAFT TO THE GATE.  NO ECAMS OCCURRED DURING THE FLIGHT.  THE LOGBOOK WAS FILLED OUT DETAILING THE AIR RETURN, BIRD STRIKE, AND THE OVERWEIGHT LANDING.

SOUTHWEST AIRLINES FLIGHT 2934 (PHL-MCO) WAS PUSHING OFF PHL GATE D2 AT APPROXIMATELY 09:45 EST ON 12/21/2009 WHEN THE PUSHBACK TUG STRUCK THE #1 ENGINE INLET COWL.  WITNESSES STATED THAT THE RAMP ALLEYWAY CONSISTED OF A COMPRESSED SNOW/ICE PACK OF APPROXIMATELY 2-3 INCHES IN DEPTH (THE RESULT OF A 20+ INCH SNOWFALL ON 12/19/2009). ON 11/29/09, AT APPROXIMATELY 07:09 MST, A FEDX DC-10 TAXIING NORTH ON H CLIPPED THE RIGHT WINGLET OF A SWAA B-737.

ON 11/29/09, AT APPROXIMATELY 07:09 MST, A FEDX DC-10 TAXIING NORTH ON H CLIPPED THE RIGHT WINGLET OF A SWAA B-737.  THE TOP HALF OF THE WINGLET WAS SEVERED OFF OF THE 737 AND THE DC-10 INCURRED MINOR DAMAGE TO THE LEADING EDGE OF THE LEFT WING SLAT APPROXIMATELY 4-5 FEET INBOARD .PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT THE SWAA #5506 REQUESTED A PUSH-BACK CLEARANCE AT GATE B13 FROM SLC ATCT.  THEY WERE INSTRUCTED "CLEARED TO PUSH, START ENGINES YOUR DISCRETION, ADVISE READY TO TAXI".  THE TUG OPERATOR PUSHED THE AIRCRAFT BACK TO AN AREA WHICH AFFORDED CLEARANCE FOR THE WINGS TO CLEAR ANY OBSTACLES AT WHICH TIME THE AIRCRAFT WAS TURNED APPROXIMATELY 90 DEGREES WHICH PLACED THE NOSE OF THE AIRCRAFT HEADING NORTH.  HOWEVER, THIS POSITION LEFT THE NOSE WHEEL ON THE LINE WHICH SEPARATES THE NON-MOVEMENT AREA (RAMP) AND TAXIWAY H. THIS PLACED THE RIGHT HALF OF THE FUSELAGE AND THE RIGHT WING PORTRUDING INTO TAXIWAY H.  APPROXIMATELY 5 MINUTES AFTER SWAA WAS ISSUED THE PUSH BACK A FEDX DC-10, FLIGHT #FDX 876 WAS CLEARED FROM THE SOUTH CARGO RAMP TO 16L VIA H.   AS THE DC-10 APPROACHED THE 737 THE CREW WAS UNAWARE THAT THE LEFT WING OF THE DC-10 DID NOT HAVE ENOUGH CLEARANCE TO MISS THE RIGHT WING OF THE 737 AND THE WINGLET ON THE 737 WAS CUT-OFF.  THE DC-10 CREW WAS UNAWARE OF THE INCIDENT UNTIL THE SWAA CREW REPORTED IT TO ATC.  THE DC-10 WAS THEN INSTRUCTED TO PROCEED TO RWY 16L AND RETURN TO THE FEDX RAMP.  THE VISUAL CONDITIONS WERE VMC BUT IT WAS FAIRLY DARK WHICH LEFT THE DC-10 CREW WITH IMPAIRED VISION.  THEY KNEW THAT THEY HAD THE CLEARANCE FOR H AND THAT ATC WOULD NOT ALLOW THEM TO PROCEED WITH THE TAXI IF THERE WAS ANYTHING THAT WOULD RESULT IN AN INCIDENT, SUCH AS OCCURRED.THE INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE ATCT WAS UNAWARE THAT, IN MANY INSTANCES, THE SWAA 737 MUST ENTER TAXI-WAY H, TO SOME EXTENT OR ANOTHER, IN ORDER TO HAVE THE CLEARANCE TO SWING THE AIRCRAFT INTO A POSITION TO REQUEST AND PROCEED FOR TAXI ON H.POST INCIDENT, SWAA, SLC ATCT AND SLC AIRPORTS, HAVE DEVELOPED A NEW PROCEDURE TO PREVENT A REOCCURRANCE OF THIS TYPE OF INCIDENT.  BASICALLY, SWAA HAS PUBLISHED INSTRUCTIONS TO THEIR CREWS THAT THEY MUST REQUEST A PUSH CLEARANCE AND TO EXPECT SOME DELAY PRIOR TO PUSH IF ANOTHER AIRCRAFT IS ON H AT WHICH TIME ATC WILL CLEAR THEM TO PUSH.DUE TO THE POSSIBLE CONFUSION ON THE PART OF THE SWAA CREW AND THE FEDX CREW AND THE LIMITED VISION PRESENT AT THE TIME AND THE SWAA CREWS BEING HANDLED AND PUSHED AS WAS CUSTOMERY FROM PAST PRACTICE, IT WAS DETERMINED NOT APPRORIATE TO VIOLATE THE CREWS OR OPERATORS. TOTAL PILOT TIME IN THE LAST YEAR HAS BEEN REQUESTED AND WILL FILE AN AMENDMENT IF IT IS RECEIVED.THIS REPORT IS RELATED TO SLC ATCT REPORT, #SLC-ATCT-031 AND SLC AIRPORT POLICE REPORT #210407.

ON DECEMBER 24, 2019, N473MC, A BOEING 747-400SF, OPERATING AS GTI8756 FROM MINNEAPOLIS-ST. PAUL INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (MSP) TO PINAL AIRPARK (MZJ) SUFFERED A POD STRIKE ON THE #4 ENGINE DURING LANDING. THE FERRY FLIGHT WAS OPERATED BY TWO (2) CREWMEMBERS, THE CAPTAIN (CA) ACTING AS PILOT FLYING (PF) AND THE FIRST OFFICER (FO) ACTING AS PILOT MONITORING (PM). GTI8756 WAS DISPATCHED IN ACCORDANCE WITH COMPANY GUIDANCE AND FAA REGULATIONS. THE FLIGHT CREW DID NOT REQUEST A BRIEFING FROM DISPATCH AND DID NOT CONTACT DISPATCH FOR ASSISTANCE IN OBTAINING UP TO DATE WEATHER EN ROUTE. THIS WAS THE CA?S FIRST OPERATION INTO MZJ. MZJ IS A VISUAL FLIGHT RULES (VFR) AIRPORT WITH NO INSTRUMENT APPROACHES OR WEATHER REPORTING TOOLS. MZJ IS A SPECIAL AIRPORT PER THE COMPANY FLIGHT OPERATIONS MANUAL (FOM), REQUIRING THE CA TO MAKE THE LANDING. THE COMPANY HAS SEEN A 23% INCREASE OF OPERATIONS INTO MZJ OVER THE LAST 12 MONTHS. A WEATHER FRONT WAS PASSING THROUGH THE AREA AS THE FLIGHT ARRIVED IN MZJ. WINDS AT AVQ, A REGIONAL AIRPORT 8.1 NM AWAY, CALLED FOR A LANDING ON RUNWAY 12. TUS APPROACH REPORTED LIGHT PRECIPITATION IN THE AREA. THE FLIGHT CREW DID NOT REFERENCE THE MZJ ASOS FOR UP TO DATE WEATHER INFORMATION. THE FLIGHT MADE THREE (3) APPROACHES, MANUALLY FLOWN WITHOUT AUTOMATION ASSISTANCE OR PROPER LATERAL AND VERTICAL GUIDANCE. THE FIRST APPROACH WAS TO RUNWAY 12, FAILING TO LINE UP WITH THE RUNWAY AND OVERSHOOTING THE TURN TO FINAL. AT 1,000 FT. ABOVE GROUND LEVEL (AGL), THE AIRCRAFT WAS 11 KNOTS ABOVE THE VREF OF 138 KNOTS, RIGHT OF CENTERLINE, AND MANEUVERING. THE CA INITIATED A GO AROUND AT 650 FT. AGL. WINDS ON THE NAVIGATION DISPLAY (ND) INDICATED A TAILWIND ON FINAL APPROACH. THE SECOND APPROACH WAS TO RUNWAY 12. WHILE IN THE TRAFFIC PATTERN, ALTITUDE VARIED BETWEEN 3,100 FT. AND 3,400 FT. AS THE CA MANUALLY FLEW. THE SECOND APPROACH WAS HIGH AND FAST, UNDERSHOOTING THE TURN TO FINAL. JUST SHORT OF THE RUNWAY THRESHOLD, AT 250 FT. AGL, THE AIRCRAFT WAS IN A 1,300 FOOT PER MINUTE (FPM) DESCENT. THE CA INITIATED A GO AROUND OVER THE RUNWAY THRESHOLD AT 180 FT. AGL. WINDS ON THE ND INDICATED A TAILWIND ON FINAL APPROACH. DURING THE THIRD AND FINAL APPROACH, THE CREW RECEIVED A ?DON?T SINK? WARNING AT A HEIGHT OF 1,282 FT. AGL AS THE CA MANUALLY FLEW THE AIRCRAFT. ONCE ESTABLISHED ON DOWNWIND FOR RUNWAY 12 SOMEONE ON THE GROUND RADIOED THE FLIGHT CREW ON THE UNICOM FREQUENCY THAT WINDS ARE FAVORING RUNWAY 30. THE FLIGHT CREW MANEUVERED FOR AN APPROACH TO RUNWAY 30 WITHOUT CONDUCTING A NEW BRIEFING, RECALCULATING PERFORMANCE, OR RUNNING THE LANDING CHECKLIST. THE TURN TO FINAL FOR RUNWAY 30 WAS MADE PAST THE EXTENDED CENTERLINE FOR RUNWAY 30, CAUSING AN OVERSHOOT. AT 1,000 FT. AGL, THE AIRCRAFT WAS 15 KNOTS ABOVE VREF, 17 DEGREES OFF THE RUNWAY HEADING, AND IN AN UNCOORDINATED TURN, THE FO DID NOT MAKE ANY REQUIRED CALLOUTS. WHEN THE AIRCRAFT CROSSED THE RUNWAY 30 THRESHOLD AT 50 FT. AGL, IT WAS NOT OVER THE PAVED RUNWAY AND AIRSPEED WAS 20 KNOTS BELOW VREF. THE CA APPLIED FULL RIGHT RUDDER TO ALIGN THE AIRCRAFT WITH THE CENTERLINE, ADDING OPPOSITE AILERON TO COUNTERACT ROLL FORCES. THE AIRCRAFT TOUCHED DOWN SIX (6) KNOTS ABOVE STALL SPEED WITH 8 DEGREES OF BANK, CAUSING THE #4 ENGINE POD TO IMPACT THE RUNWAY. THIS EVENT OCCURRED AFTER THE CREW FLEW THREE (3) UNSTABLE APPROACHES WITHOUT VERTICAL GUIDANCE OR THE ASSISTANCE OF AUTOMATION. THE CREW WAS UNFAMILIAR WITH THE VFR ONLY AIRPORT AND ARRIVED DURING A FRONTAL PASSAGE. THE CREW WAS UNABLE TO IDENTIFY THE CHANGING WEATHER CONDITIONS AND ADJUST THEIR APPROACH PLAN ACCORDINGLY.

THIS WAS CONFIRMED BY A COMPANY MECHANIC, SEATED IN ROW 10A ONBOARD THE AIRCRAFT. THE MECHANIC DIRECTED THE PASSENGER NOT TO EXIT THE AIRCRAFT THROUGH THE DITCHING DAM HATCH AND TO PROCEED TO THE MAIN AIR-STAIRS DOOR AS INITIALLY INSTRUCTED.  THE MECHANIC THEN TURNED HIS ATTENTION TO AND ASSISTED A LADY (BLIND) WITH HER SERVICE DOG APPROXIMATELY TWO ROWS FORWARD OF HIM EXIT THE AIRCRAFT.  A FEW PASSENGERS IN THE REAR OF THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN TO PANIC AND TWO PASSENGERS EXITED THE AIRCRAFT THROUGH THE OPEN DITCHING DAM HATCH; ONE PASSENGER APPARENTLY CUT THEIR FINGER (MINOR) ON THE AIRCRAFT. TWO AVIATION SAFETY INSPECTORS (ASI), WERE DISPATCHED TO THE SCENE OF THE INCIDENT TO INVESTIGATE AT 09:35 LOCAL (13:35 ZULU).    UPON ARRIVING ON SCENE, ASIS CONFIRMED THE INITIAL REPORTS FROM THE ROC.  THEY ALSO CONFIRMED THAT ALL 43 PASSENGERS AND 3 CREW MEMBERS WERE EVACUATED WITHOUT INJURIES.  REASON FOR THE EVACUATION: THE FLIGHT CREW REPORTED THAT, DURING THEIR DESCENT FOR LANDING AT THE WASHINGTON NATIONAL, D.C. AIRPORT (DCA), AT FL 230,  WHILE COMPLYING WITH AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL (ATC) INSTRUCTIONS TO REDUCE SPEED, THEY RECEIVED A FLIGHT DECK WARNING OF SMOKE IN THE LAVATORY.  WHEN THE FLIGHT CREW NOTIFIED THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT OF THE WARNING, SHE REPORTED THAT SHE HAD SEEN WHAT APPEARED TO BE SMOKE IN THE REAR SECTION OF THE CABIN AND CHECKED THE LAVATORY FOR SMOKE OR FIRE.  SHE FELT THE DOOR FOR HEAT AND, FEELING NONE,  OPENED IT.  SHE FOUND NO EVIDENCE OF SMOKE OR FIRE INSIDE THE LAVATORY.  FAA INSPECTORS REPORTED NO SIGNS OF FIRE DURING THEIR INVESTIGATION.   WHO INITIATED THE EVACUATION?: THE CAPTAIN INSTRUCTED THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT TO PREPARE FOR AN EMERGENCY LANDING AT PHL AND AN EVACUATION ON THE RUNWAY.  WHICH EXITS WERE USED?: BOTH OVER-WING EMERGENCY EXITS WERE OPENED, HOWEVER PASSENGER EGRESS ONLY OCCURRED OVER THE LEFT WING. THE MAJORITY OF PASSENGERS EXITED THROUGH THE MAIN CABIN DOOR. THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT DIRECTED PASSENGERS TO THE MAIN EXIT BECAUSE THERE WAS NO RESIDUAL EVIDENCE OF SMOKE OR FIRE IN THE LAVATORY OR THE AFT CABIN.  THE GALLEY DOOR WAS NOT USED.    WHICH EXITS MANFUNCTIONED?: NONE  ESTIMATED TOTAL TIME OF THE EVACUATION?: PASSENGERS EXITED THE AIRCRAFT IN APPROXIMATELY FIVE MINUTES IN AN ORDERLY AND CALM MANNER. THEY WERE BUSSED TO THE PHL TERMINAL.  NATURE AND EXTENT OF INJURIES?: THE LANDING AND EVACUATION OF PASSENGERS AND CREW ON PHL RWY 27L WAS ENEVENTFUL. NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED.  THE FLIGHT CREW REPORTED THAT MAINTENANCE WAS PERFORMED ON THE AIRCRAFT THE PREVIOUS NIGHT AS A RESULT OF A LAVATORY SMOKE INDICATION. THIS WAS CONFIRMED BY THE PRINCIPAL INSPECTORS FROM THE PSA CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT OFFICE (CMO). INVESTIGATION CONTINUES INTO REPORTS OF MULTIPLE CARBON SEAL FAILURES.

THE CREW WAS CLEARED TO TAXI ON A TAXIWAY WHERE AIRCRAFT ARE PARKED IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE TAXIWAY. THE CAPTAIN SAW THAT THE TAIL OF AN US AIR AIRCRAFT WAS VERY CLOSE TO THE TAXIWAY. HE CHOSE TO MOVE OFF THE YELLOW LINE AND THOUGHT HE HAD CLEARANCE TO PASS THE AIRCRAFT. THE CREW THOUGHT THEY HAD CLEARED THE TAIL AND DID NOT BELIEVE THEY HAD STRUCK THE OTHER AIRCRAFT. AFTER PARKING AT THE GATE BOTH CREWMEMBERS DID AN EXTERIOR INSPECTION TO SEE IF THERE HAD BEEN ANY INDICATION AF HITTING THE OTHER AIRCRAFT AND DID NOT SEE ANY DAMAGE. DAMAGE TO THE OTHER AIRCRAFT WAS FOUND BY US AIR PERSONNEL WHO WERE ON THAT AIRCRAFT WHEN IT WAS STRUCK BY THE SPIRIT AIRCRAFT. THE US AIR AIRCRAFT WAS NOT PROPERLY PARKED AND BROWARD COUNTY AVIATION DEPARTMENT(BCAD) OFFICIALS WERE NOT AWARE THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS IN THAT AREA. BCAD IS SUPPOSED TO BE NOTIFIED BY THE AIRLINES WHEN AIRCRAFT ARE BEING PARKED THERE SO THAT THE FLL TOWER CAN BE MADE AWARE OF THE SITUATION. TOWER WAS NOT AWARE THAT AN AIRCRAFT WAS PARKED IMPROPERLY. BCAD CLOSED THE TAXIWAY AFTER THIS INCIDENT. THIS TAXIWAY SHOULD HAVE BEEN CLOSED PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT. BOTH SPIRIT CREWMEMBERS HAVE FILED ASAP REPORTS AND THIS INCIDENT HAS BEEN INVESTIGATED BY THE ASAP ERC.

THE CAPTAIN RESPONDED AND TOLD FA1 HE WOULD GET BACK TO HIM. FA1 ALERTED THE AFT FLIGHT ATTENDANTS AND THE ATTENDANTS CHECKED THE LAVATORIES PER THEIR FIRE FIGHTING PROCEDURES. THE CAPTAIN CALLED TO THE CABIN AND TOLD THEM THEY COULD NOT FIND ANYTHING WRONG BUT WERE RETURNING TO THE GATE SO THAT MAINTENANCE COULD INSPECT THE AIRCRAFT. TAXIING BACK TO THE GATE THE AFT FLIGHT ATTENDANT ALERTED FA1 THAT HE COULD SEE A MIST IN THE CABIN. FA2 CALLED THE CAPTAIN AND REPORTED THE HAZE. AT THIS TIME FA1 NOTICED THE FOG/SMOKE IN THE CABIN AND ALSO INFORMED THE CAPTAIN. THE CAPTAIN ADVISED TO EVACUATE THE AIRCRAFT USING THE FORWARD DOORS AND TAILCONE. HE TAXIED TO THE AREA NEAR THE FIRE STATION, STOPPED THE AIRCRAFT AND ISSUED THE EVACUATION. THE AFT FLIGHT ATTENDANT OPENED THE DOOR TO THE TAILCONE. THE TAILCONE DEPLOYED BUT THE SLIDE PACK DID NOT FALL AND DEPLOY THE SLIDE. THE FA PUSHED THE CONTAINER HOUSING THE TAILCONE SLIDE OUT AND THE SLIDE DEPLOYED AUTOMATICALLY. FA3 OPENED THE 1R AND STARTED HER EVACUATION. FA1 OPENED THE 1L BUT THE SLIDE DID NOT DEPLOY AUTOMATICALLY SO HE REACHED DOWN AND PULLED THE MANUAL INFLATION HANDLE. HE CALLED THE PASSENGERS TO HIS DOOR AND AS THE FIRST PERSON APPROACHED HE HEARD A POPPING SOUND AND LOOKED TO SEE THAT THE SLIDE DEFLATED. HE BLOCKED HIS EXIT AND REDIRECTED THE PASSENGERS TO 1R. ONCE ALL THE PASSENGERS HAD EVACUATED THE CREW NOTICED THAT THERE WAS NO SMOKE BUT THAT THE AREA BEHIND THE AFT LAVATORIES WERE HOT. THERE WAS NO UNUSUAL SMELL OR SMOKE. THE CREW EVACUATED, GATHERED THE PASSENGERS AND DID A HEAD COUNT OF 144+1. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT BOUGHT OUT WATER AND GATORADE AND THE EMTS WERE AVAILABLE TO ASSIST PASSENGERS. THE CREW OF AIRCRAFT N7887A REALIZED THEIR AIRCRAFT HAD BEEN HIT AND COMMUNICATED WITH THE TOW-TRACTOR (NON-VERBAL-SIGNAL) TO TOW THE AIRCRAFT BACK TO THE GATE (C13) FOR JETWAY ACCESS. AIRCRAFT N243WN BEGAN TO TAXI INITIATING A RIGHT TURN AWAY FROM AIRCRAFT N7887A. OPERATIONAL FACTORS, THE GROUND CREW PUSHED AIRPLANE FROM GATE 13 AND PARKED IN POSITION THAT COMPANY AIRPLANE (N243WN) HAD INADEQUATE WINGTIP CLEARANCE TO TAXI TO AVOID COLLISION. NIGHT-TIME-CONDITIONS AND THE RAIN MAY HAVE REDUCED VISIBILITY CONTRIBUTING TO GROUND CREW & COCKPIT CREW (N243WN) VISIBILITY. MASSPORT BOSTON OPERATIONS ACCIDENT REPORT STATED: UPON MY ARRIVAL (MASSPORT OPERATIONS ALAN WADE) I FOUND AN AMERICAN EAGLE SAAB 340B, FLIGHT 4998 INBOUND FROM YUL (MONTREAL CANADA) WITH ITS BELLY SLICED OPEN. THE "DORSAL FIN" IS MOUNTED IN FRONT OF THE CONTROLS TO PREVENT LUGGAGE OR OFF LOADED CARGO FROM STRIKING THE SHIFT LEVER OR THROTTLE CONTROLS. THE "DORSAL FIN" IS LOCATED JUST FORWARD AND TO THE RIGHT OF THE OPERATOR. THESE STATEMENTS ARE AVAILABLE FOR REVIEW AT THE FAA UNITED AIRLINES SAN FRANCISCO CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT OFFICE (SFO-CMO). UAL FLIGHT 862, A B747-400, WAS A SCHEDULE FLIGHT FROM SIDNEY, AUSTRALIA TO SAN FRANCISCO, CA ON MAY 1, 2002. APPROXIMATELY 2.5 HOURS FROM, AND 1000 MILES NORTHEAST OF, SIDNEY, AUSTRALIA, THE FLIGHT EXPERIENCED SEVERE TURBULENCE, WHICH RESULTED IN INJURY TO TWO (2) FLIGHT ATTENDANTS AND FIVE (5) PASSENGERS. THE AIRCRAFT DIVERTED TO AUCKLAND, NEW ZEALAND AND MADE AN UNEVENTFUL LANDING. AS THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS WERE MAKING THEIR WAY THROUGH THE CABIN TO ENSURE ALL THE PASSENGERS HAD BUCKLED THEIR SEATBELTS, THE CAPTAIN MADE AN ANNOUNCEMENT FOR THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS TO TAKE THEIR SEATS AND FASTEN THEIR SEATBELTS. ONE CREWMEMBER INDICATED THAT THE TOTAL TIME WAS PROBABLY ONLY 10-15 SECONDS. EACH STATEMENT INDICATES THAT THERE WAS VERY LITTLE TIME TO PREPARE EVERYONE FOR WHAT WAS TO FOLLOW.

THE CREW REQUESTED A TURN TO THE LEFT (DIRECT TO LRP) TO AVOID THE BUILD UP AND GO THROUGH AN AREA OF LITTLE TO NO PRECIPITATION. THE REQUEST WAS DENIED TWICE. UPON SWITCHING FREQUENCIES TO 120.85 (NY APP) THE LEFT TURN REQUEST TO LRP WAS GRANTED. THE CREW CHANGED HEADING TO GO DIRECT TO THE LRP VOR. THE CREW THEN LEVELED OFF AT 14,000 FEET.  UPON REACHING 14000 THE CREW BEGAN TO FLY INTO LIGHT PRECIPITATION, THE ICING EQUIPMENT WAS THEN TURNED ON. THE CAPTAIN THEN  NOTICED A VERY RAPID CHANGE IN THE OAT. THE TEMPERATURE DROPPED FROM -1C TO -17 C IN LESS THAN 10 SECONDS. THE CAPTAIN THEN LOOKED OVER HIS SHOULDER AT THE WING AND SAW THE AIRPLANE GATHERING ICE EXTREMELY QUICKLY. BEFORE THE FLIGHT CREW COULD REACT, THEY NOTICED THE AIRSPEED PLUMMETING TO ZERO. THE PITOT HEAT 1 AND 2 CAUTION LIGHTS THEN ILLUMINATED. THE FLIGHT CREW IMMEDIATELY REQUESTED A LOWER ALTITUDE WHILE DECLARING AN EMERGENCY FOR ENCOUNTERING SEVERE ICING. A DESCENT WAS GIVEN TO 12,000 FEET. AT 12,000 FEET, THE CREW STATED THE AIRPLANE WAS STILL PICKING UP ICE, WITH ZERO AIRSPEED INDICATED. THE CREW THEN DESCENDED TO 8,000 FEET WHERE THEY BROKE OUT OF THE CLOUDS AND ENCOUNTERED POSITIVE AIR TEMPERATURES. SHORTLY AFTER, THE ICE BLOCKING THE PITOT TUBES BROKE OFF AND AIRSPEED INDICATIONS RETURNED. THE FLIGHT LANDED OVERWEIGHT, BUT WITHOUT INCIDENT.

BRADLEY OPERATIONS EXTENDED THE JET BRIDGE HOURS PRIOR TO THE ARRIVAL OF FLIGHT NUMBER 4233 AND THEN NOTIFIED THE RAMP PERSONNEL OF THE EXTENSION OF THE JET BRIDGE TO FACILITATE THE DRYING PROCESS. PROPER NOTIFICATION FROM THE AIR CARRIERS RECEIVING RAMP SUPERVISOR TO THE GROUND RAMP PERSONNEL DID NOT OCCUR PRIOR TO THE ARRIVAL OF THE FLIGHT. THIS CAUSED THE JET WAY TO REMAIN IN THE EXTENDED POSITION DURING THE TAXI IN OF THE AIRCRAFT. FLIGHT CREW APPROACHED THE GATE AT NIGHT, IN HEAVY RAIN, TO ASSUME THE GATE WAS PROPERLY POSITIONED AND FOLLOWED THE RAMP PERSONNEL?S INSTRUCTIONS FOR PARKING. THE LEFT WING SLAT SUBSEQUENTLY CAME IN CONTACT WITH THE JET WAY CAUSING A PUNCTURE IN THE SLAT. NO INJURIES AND MINOR DAMAGE RESULTED TO THE LEFT WING SLAT WHICH WAS SUBSEQUENTLY REMOVED AND REPLACED THE NEXT DAY WITH THE OUTBOUND FLIGHT BEING CANCELLED AS A RESULT. FURTHER THE POI FOR THE CARRIER, WILL DETERMINE THE COURSE OF ACTION FOR THE FLIGHT CREW AFTER IT PROCESSES THROUGH THE CARRIERS ASAP COMMITTEE. HEAVY RAIN, NIGHT CONDITIONS, LACK OF COMMUNICATION, IMPROPER JET BRIDGE MAINTENANCE, RUSHING, AND THE LACK OF CREW SITUATIONAL AWARENESS WERE ALL CONTRIBUTING FACTORS TO THIS INCIDENT.

DURING LANDING ROLLOUT PASSENGERS BEGAN YELLING "FIRE" AND POINTING TOWARDS THE FLOOR OF THE AIRCRAFT.  THE SOLE FLIGHT ATTENDANT SEATED IN HIS FORWARD JUMPSEAT HEARD A "POP" SOUND. HE OBSERVED SMOKE AND "A FLAME" UNDER PASSENGER SEAT 1D. HE IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIED THE FLIGHT DECK OF FIRE AND SMOKE IN THE CABIN AND BEGAN FIGHTING THE FIRE WITH A HALON EXTINGUISHER. THE FLIGHT CREW STOPPED THE AIRCRAFT AND ORDERED AN EMERGENCY EVACUATION  OVER THE PA (PUBLIC ADDRESS SYSTEM). PASSENGERS SEATED IN THE EMERGENCY EXIT ROW OPENED THE OVERWING EXITS AND BEGAN EVACUATING THE AIRCRAFT. AT THE SAME TIME, THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT EXTINGUISHED THE FIRE AND OPENED THE FORWARD PASSENGER ENTRY DOOR. THE REMAINING PASSENGERS AND CREW EVACUATED THE AIRCRAFT THROUGH THE FOWARD PASSENGER ENTRY DOOR. ALL PASSENGERS AND CREW EVACUATED WITH NO INJURIES.   IT WAS LATER DETERMINED THAT THE CAUSE OF FIRE AND SMOKE IN THE CABIN WAS FROM A SPARE E-CIGARETTE BATTERY (LITHIUM ION) LOCATED IN A PASSENGER'S CARRY ON BAG. FIRE AND SMOKE IN THE CABIN.  2. WHO INITIATED EVACUATION?  FLIGHT DECK OVER THE PA (PUBLIC ADDRESS SYSTEM) FOLLOWED BY FLIGHT ATTENDANT AFTER EXTINGUISHING THE FIRE.  3. WHICH EXITS (BY SPECIFIC LOCATION) WERE USED, WHICH WERE NOT, AND REASON FOR NON-USE? BOTH OVERWING EXITS WERE USED AND THE FORWARD PASSENGER ENTRY DOOR WAS USED. THE AFT SERVICE DOOR WAS NOT NEEDED BECAUSE ALL PASSENGERS EVACUATED FROM OVERWING EXITS AND FORWARD PASSENGER ENTRY DOOR.  4. WHETHER ANY EXIT SLIDES, OR ASSOCIATE COMPONENTS MALFUNCTIONED AND, IF SO, WHAT WERE THE MALFUNCTIONS. THERE WERE NO SLIDE OR EXIT MALFUNCTIONS.  5. WHETHER ANY PARTICULAR EXIT WAS USED BY THE MAJORITY OF EVACUEES AND, IF SO, WHY? THE MAJORITY OF PASSENGERS EXITED THROUGH THE OVERWING EXITS DUE TO THE FIRE BEING IN THE FRONT OF THE AIRCRAFT.  6. INCIDENT NARRATIVEON JULY 29, 2011 AT 7:45PM CDT THE DUTY STANDBY INSPECTOR FOR THE CHICAGO O'HARE FLIGHT STANDARDS DISTRICT OFFICE RECEIVED A TELEPHONE CALL FROM THE GREAT LAKES REGIONAL CONTROL CENTER TO REPORT THAT A DELTA AIRLINES AIRCRAFT AT THE CHICAGO O'HARE E-TERMINAL HAD STRUCK ANOTHER DELTA AIRCRAFT DURING PUSH BACK.   THERE WERE NO REPORTED INJURIES TO ANY OF THE PASSENGERS. THAT INSPECTOR RESPONDED TO THE INCIDENT REPORT BY TRAVELING TO THE SCENE TO CONDUCT AN INVESTIGATION. ON ARRIVAL AT THE CHICAGO O'HARE E-TERMINAL GATES, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT DELTA AIRLINES, MD-88 AIRCRAFT, REGISTRATION NUMBER N970DL, FLIGHT NUMBER 1777, ORD TO ATL WITH 76 PASSENGER AND 5 CREW MEMBERS HAD BEEN PUSHED BACK FROM GATE E-13  INTO DELTA AIRLINES A-319 AIRCRAFT, REGISTRATION NUMBER N332NB, FLIGHT NUMBER 2207 WITH 129 PASSENGERS AND 5 CREWMEMBERS. DURING THE COURSE OF THIS INVESTIGATION IT WAS DETERMINED THAT AIRCRAFT N332NB HAD BEEN PUSHED BACK FROM TERMINAL GATE E-15 AND HAD REQUESTED TAXI INSTRUCTIONS FROM GROUND CONTROL. THAT DAMAGE INCLUDED A FUSELAGE PUNCTURE ABOUT 10 INCHES IN LENGTH AND OTHER SURFACE DISTORTION. AIRCRAFT N332NB SUSTAINED DAMAGE TO THE RIGHT WING TIP FAIRING OR WINGLET. DELTA AIRLINES MAINTENANCE REMOVED THE DAMAGED RIGHT WING FAIRING (WINGLET) FROM N332NB AND DEFERRED IT PER THE CDL. THE AIRCRAFT DEPARTED IN REVENUE SERVICE THE FOLLOWING MORNING. THE MD-88 AIRCRAFT, N970DL WAS TAKEN TO THE OLD NORTHWEST HANGAR TO AWAIT A MAINTENANCE CREW.THE DELTA AIRLINES TUG OPERATOR WAS SUBSEQUENTLY TESTED FOR DRUGS AND ALCOHOL. THE RESULTS OF THOSE TEST WERE NEGATIVE. AT THE PRESENT TIME DELTA AIRLINES CONTINUES WITH THEIR INTERNAL INVESTIGATION OF THIS INCIDENT AND HAVE NOT FORMULATED A CORRECTIVE ACTION PLAN.THE DELTA AIRLINES MAINTENANCE TEAM THAT ARRIVED AT ORD SHORTLY AFTER THIS INCIDENT COMPLETED THE REPAIRS TO AIRCRAFT N970DL ON AUGUST 8, 2011. ALL WORK WAS DOCUMENT ON NON ROUTINE LOG FORMS AND ALL OPERATIONAL AND FUNCTIONAL CHECK WERE ACCOMPLISHED. IN ADDITION THE (RII) REQUIRED INSPECTIONS WERE ACCOMPLISHED AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS RELEASED FOR SERVICE AND FERRIED OUT OF ORD ON AUGUST 9, 2011.

ON MARCH 3, 2012 AT APPROXIMATELY 1237 EST A DELTA MD-88 FLIGHT 181 FROM LAGUARIDA WAS TAXING TO THE MCNAMARA TERMI

ON MARCH 3, 2012 AT APPROXIMATELY 1237 EST A DELTA MD-88 FLIGHT 181 FROM LAGUARIDA WAS TAXING TO THE MCNAMARA TERMINAL GATE A-51.  IT WAS ON THE OUTER TAXI LINE (UNIFORM 7) PASSING BY THE FLEET SERVICE BUILDING, # 820 AND STRUCK A BUS THAT HAD BEEN PARKED OUT SIDE THE ZIPPER LINE AT THE BUILDING.  THE AIRCRAFT LEFT WING TIP AND NUMBER 5 SLAT HIT THE BUS, WHICH WAS OVER TURNED AS THE AIRCRAFT TAXIED.  THE CREW STOPPED THE AIRCRAFT AND NOTED SOMETHING WRONG AND MADE A CALL REQUESTING MAINTENANCE TO COME LOOK AT THE AIRCRAFT PRIOR TO FURTHER TAXI (SUSPECTING A BLOWN TIRE).  MAINTENANCE CAME TO THE AIRCRAFT AND NOTED THE BUS THAT WAS ON ITS SIDE, THE LEFT WING TIP DAMAGE, AND DAMAGE TO THE NUMBER 5 SLAT.WAYNE METRO AIRPORT POLICE PERFORMED INTERVIEWS WITH THE BUS DRIVER, BOTH THE FLIGHT AND CABIN CREW.  THE BUS DRIVER INDICATED HE HAD PARKED THE BUS OUT SIDE THE ZIPPER LINE (AN UNAUTHORIZED LOCATION) TO GO INTO BUILDING # 820 FOR A RESTROOM BREAK.  WHEN HE LEFT THE BUS HE DID NOT NOTICE ANY AIRCRAFT MOVEMENT ON THE RAMP.  UPON HIS RETURN HE NOTED THE BUS ON ITS SIDE AND SHORTLY THERE AFTER, EMERGENCY PERSONNEL RESPONDING.  THE BUS WAS A 2006 CHAMPION PASSENGER BUS REGISTERED TO METOR CARS INC., IN TAYLOR, MICHIGAN.  THE BUS SUSTAINED MULTIPLE AREAS OF DAMAGE, AND HAD A LARGE GOUGE NEAR THE TOP REAR DRIVER'S SIDE, ALONG WITH DAMAGE TO THE PASSENGER'S SIDE.  THE DAMAGE TO THE LEFT SIDE OF THE BUS INCREASES GOING AFT, THE DIRECTION THE AIRCRAFT WAS TRAVELING.  THE WINDSHIELD WAS ALSO BROKEN; IN ADDITION THERE WAS FUEL AND OIL SPILLED.  THERE WERE NO PASSENGERS ON THE BUS AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT.THE FLIGHT HAD BEEN CLEARED TO TAXI IN ON U7, THE ORIGINAL GATE ASSIGNED WAS A53 BUT IT WAS OCCUPIED THUS WAS CHANGE TO A51.  DURING THE TAXI IN THE FIRST OFFICER WAS STARTING THE APU.  PRIOR TO STOPPING THE AIRCRAFT BOTH THE CAPTAIN AND FIRST OFFICER INDICATED FEELING A "THUMP" AND THE AIRCRAFT YAWED LEFT.  NONE OF THE THREE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS ON THE AIRCRAFT OBSERVE THE INCIDENT, BUT DID DESCRIBE THE SOUND AND FEELING OF HITTING A POTHOLE.  THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT IN THE FORWARD POSITION DID NOT FEEL THE AIRCRAFT  YAW AFTER THE IMPACT; HOWEVER DID HEAR THE IMPACT.  THE OTHER TWO FLIGHT ATTENDANTS WERE SEATED IN THE AFT OF THE AIRCRAFT AND INDICATED THAT THY FELT THE AIRCRAFT GO LEFT UPON IMPACT.ALL THREE INDICATED THAT NONE OF THE PASSENGERS MADE ANY COMPLAINTS OF INJURIES.THE INSPECTOR ON SITE OF THE INCIDENT WAS THE FIRST CONTACTED ABLE TO PERFORM ON SITE DUTIES.  THE INVESTIGATION WAS PASSED ON TO A DIFFERENT INSPECTOR ON MONDAY THE 5TH OF MARCH 2012.CORRESPONDENCE WITH THE NTSB INVESTIGATOR INDICATED THAT THE DAMAGE WAS NOT SUBSTANTIAL PER PART 830, THUS AN INCIDENT.  NTSB ID IS DCA 12 NA 037.

THE SCHEDULED PASSENGER FLIGHT WAS CONDUCTED UNDER 14 CFR PART 121.                                    THE CAPTAIN STATED THAT HE CONDUCTED A CREW BRIEFING PRIOR TO BOARDING THE AIRPLANE.  STARTUP AND TAXI WERE NORMAL, AND DURING THE TAXI, THE CAPTAIN AGAIN BRIEFED THE COCKPIT CREW, AND INCLUDED ENGINE FAILURES AND NON-REJECT SITUATIONS.  THE AIRPLANE LINED UP ON RUNWAY 04L, AND THE CAPTAIN APPLIED TAKEOFF POWER SLOWLY AND SMOOTHLY.  AT TAKEOFF DECISION SPEED (V1), THERE WAS A LOUD EXPLOSION.  A WHITE "ENGINE FAIL" LIGHT ILLUMINATED IN FRONT OF TH                                                                            E CAPTAIN, AND THE NUMBER 1 ENGINE N1 DECREASED BY 30%. NUMBER 2 AND 3 ENGINES APPEARED NORMAL. THE CAPTAIN CONTINUED THE TAKEOFF, AN THE LANDING GEAR WAS RAISED. A RED, LEFT MAIN LANDING GEAR WARDNING LIGHT ILLUMINATED ON THE FRONT PANEL. TEH AIRPLANE TURNED TO A HEADING OF 010 AND SLOWLY CLIMBED TO 3,000 FEET. DURING THE CLIMB, AN AIRFRAME VIBRATION DEVELOPED. AFTER LEVEL-OFF, THE CREW BEGAN TO TROUBLESHOOT THE EMERGENCY, AND FOUND THAT WHEN THE NUMBER 3 ENGINE N1 WAS REDUCED TO ABOUT 25 PERCENT, THE VIBRATION DISAPPEARED. BOTH THE NUMBER 1 AND THE NUMBER 3 ENGINES REMAINED AT APPROX. 25 PERCENT N1 FOR THE REST OF THE FLIGHT. AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL PROVIDED VECTORS FOR A RETURN TO NEWARK. DURING THE RETURN, THE CREW DUMPED ABOUT 90,000 POUNDS OF FUEL. THE CREW ALSO RAN BOTH 1-ENGINE, AND 2-ENGINE INOPERATIVE CHECKLISTS, AND PREPARED DATA CARDS FOR BOTH SCARIOUS. THE CAPTAIN FLEW THE ILS GLIDESCOPE DOWN TO A  FULL-STOP LANDING, ON RUNWAY 04R. THE ACARS RECORDED THE LANDING AT 2016. AFTER THE INITIAL STOP, THE BRAKES WOULD NOT RELEASE  SO THE CREW SHUT DOWN THE ENGINES ON THE RUNWAY, AND THE PASSENGERS AND CREW DISEMBARKED THROUGH THE NORMAL DEPLANING DOORS. THE MAJORITY OF NOZZLE MATERIAL WAS FOUND ON THE DEPARTURE RUNWAY, HOWEVER, ONE NOZZLE SEGMENT WAS FOUND IN THE LEFT MAIN LANDING GEAR WHELL WELL. ONE OF THE EIGHT ANTI-ROTATION NOZZLE LOCKS WAS RECOVERED. THE THREADED STUD FROM THAT LOCK HAD BEEN SHEARED FROM THE PLATE, AND THE ENGAGEMENT TANGS EXHIBITED WEAR AND DAMAGE. THE FIRST STAGE LOW PRESSURE TURBLINE BLADES HAD MINOR TRAILING EDGE AIRFOIL DAMAGE, AND THE SECOND STAGE    LOW PRESSURE TURBINE BLADES EXHIBITED CIRCUMFERENTIAL RUB MARKS ON THE INNER PLATFORM LEADING EDGE, AND ON THE AIRFOILS NEAR THE BLADE. AS AN ACTION IN THE FLIGHT MANUAL IRREGULAR PROCEDURE, THE FIRST OFFICER ATTEMPTED TO TURN OFF THE POWER TRANSFER UNIT (PTU), HOWEVER, THE PTU WOULD NOT SHUT OFF.  THE FIRST OFFICER CONTACTED SAMC WHO INSTRUCTED HIM TO CYCLE THE CIRCUIT BREAKER FOR THE PTU.  THIS HAD NO AFFECT AND THE PTU CONTINUED TO RUN UNTIL THE YELLOW HYDRAULIC SYSTEM OVERHEATED.  THE FLIGHT CREW TURNED OFF THE YELLOW SYSTEM, WHICH NOW FORCED THEM TO RELY SOLELY ON THE BLUE HYDRAULIC SYSTEM WHICH REQUIRED THEM TO LAND AS-SOON-AS-POSSIBLE.  THE FLIGHT CREW ATTEMPTED TO LOWER THE FLAPS AFTER LETTING THE YELLOW SYSTEM COOL DOWN; HOWEVER, THE FLAPS LOCKED OUT BEFORE FULLY DEPLOYING.  THE LANDING GEAR WAS EXTENDED MANUALLY AND THE AUXILIARY POWER UNIT (APU) WAS STARTED ON SHORT FINAL.  THE AIRCRAFT LANDED WITHOUT INCIDENT AT KPIT.
